Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: Ilwvm.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION NO. oz DIR. ARNEL M. AGABE 04 JUL 2019 Regional Director DILG Regional Office X Km. 3, Masterson Avenue, Upper Carmen Cagayan de Oro City Dear Dir. Agabe: s. 202 This is in reference to the letter dated 7 March 2019 of Dir. Docallos of DILG Cagayan de Oro City which was indorsed to this level on 21 March 2019, seeking this Department's guidance on whether a government employee can assume as Sangguniang Kabataan Chairperson. This query arose from the case of Ms. Kiranjit Kaur Aldeguer, an elected Sangguniang Kabataan Member of Barangay Cugman, Cagayan de Oro, but who succeeded and proclaimed by the Commission on Elections (COMELEC) as SK Chairperson due to the disqualification (overaged) of the elected SK Chairperson. In your letter, you also informed this level that prior to the COMELEC proclamation, Ms. Aldeguer was already employed at the Department of Education (DepEd) as a teacher with regular item (information was given by Ms. Aldeguer herself during her visit to Dir. Docallos' Office). In consideration of the given facts, at the outset, this Department opines that Ms. Aldeguer is not allowed to hold two positions in the government. This is our settled stand, consistent with the Article IX (B)(7)1 and (8)2 of the 1987 Philippine Constitution and SECTION 7. No elective official shall be eligible for appointment or designation in any capacity to any public office or position during his tenure. Unless otherwise allowed by law or by the primary functions of his position, no appointive official shall hold any other office Or employment in the Government or any subdivision, agency or instrumentality thereof, including government-owned or controlled corporations or their subsidiaries. 2 SECTION 8. NO elective or appointive public officer or employee shall receive additional, double, or indirect compensation, unless specifically authorized by law, nor accept without the consent of the Congress, any present, emolument, office, or title Of any kind from any foreign government.

bolstered by Rule XII of the 2017 Omnibus Rules on Appointments and Other Human Resource Actions, Revised 2018, which provides: Sec. 117, No appointive ofFcial shall hold any other office or employment in the government unless otherwise allowed by law or by the primary functions of his/her position. Sec. 118. No elective official shall be eligible for appointment in any capacity to any public office or position during his/her tenure. Sec. 119. No elective or appointive public officer or employee shall receive additional, double or indirect compensation, unless specifically authorized by law, nor accept without consent of' Congress, any present, emolument, office or title of any kind from foreign government. Pensions and gratuities shall not be considered as additional, double or indirect compensation. Thus, no less that the Philippine Constitution and CSC issuance mandate that an elective or appointive official is prohibited to hold any other office in the government or eligible for appointment, unless the same is allowed by law, It was also stated in the letter that the father of Ms. Aldeguer, Mr. James Lee Bation, went to DILG Central Office and talked to Usec. Densing and also to Atty. Pedregosa of the Legal and Legislative Liaison Service (LLLS). Mr. Bation claimed that he was advised by Atty. Pedregosa that there is no legal impediment for Ms. Aldeguer to assume the Office of SK Chairperson notwithstanding her permanent employment with DepEd. The Central Office disagrees with Mr. Bation's claim. We opine that his statements were tainted with lies and untruthfulness. Upon verification with Atty. Pedregosa, Mr. Bation was advised that holding of said positions are not allowed and Ms. Aldeguer has to choose between the two government positions. It was also explained to Mr. Bation the nature of honorarium of SK Chairperson as ex officio Sanggunian member, and receiving the same, together with the salary of a public school teacher will tantamount to double compensation. It was where Atty. Pedregosa provided him a copy of DILG Opinion No. 13 s. 2011 which only pertains to the honorarium of a Board of Director and at the same time member of the House of Representative. It must be noted that there is big a difference in the situation in the herein opinion and the present case, as honorarium received by the SK Chairpe rson cannot be Pensions or gratuities shall not be considered as additional. double, or indirect compensation. Page 2 of 4

considered as an additional compensation, but as the only compensation given for services rendered3; unlike the above-mentioned opinion wherein being a member of a Board of Director is an addition to the work of the official who is a member of the House of Representative, thus receipt of honorarium is proper in the situation described in the above-cited opinion but not in the case of SK Chairperson. In fact, Mr. Bation again returned to LLLS and was assisted by Atty. Octavo, where the latter also counselled him that the holding Of two positions in the government is not allowed, citing pertinent laws and opinion of this Department. However, Mr. Bation appears to be unreceptive of the advice and will not believe Atty. Octavo. He insisted that such situation is allowed as the SK is only receiving an honorarium, clinging to DILG Opinion No. 13, s. 2011 as basis. Other than the explanation above on the honorarium, what Mr. Bation failed to realize is that this case does not mainly dwells with issue Of salary and honorarium but the situation wherein a public official is holding two different positions in the government, which is explicitly prohibited by no less than the 1987 Philippine Constitution. His strong asseverations pertaining to the receipt of honorarium and salary does not only show of his failure to understand the situation but also his rejection of the advice given to him and to Ms. Aldeguer by this Department. Meanwhile, it was stated in the letter that Ms. Aldeguer was already appointed as public school teacher prior to her proclamation as SK Chairperson. Thus, it follows that at the time of proclamation, she is already holding an appointive position in the government. Given the same situation, upon proclamation as SK Chairperson, she has the option to choose which position in the government she will prefer. If she prefers to remain as a school teacher, she should have not taken her oath and should not have assumed the position of SK Chairperson. Otherwise, if she choose to serve as an SK Chairperson, she should have resigned from her position as public school teacher. Holding of two government positions will tantamount to violation of the above cited supreme law and CSC rules, and can be a basis of an administrative case against Ms. Aldeguer. Please note that that this latin maxim still holds true, "Ignorantia legis neminem excusat"or "Ignorance of the law excuses no one': Much more is expected from a public school teacher who should have the understanding of the Constitution and CSC rules as government servant. As far as this level is concerned, Ms. Aldeguer was properly advised by DILG field offices and also by the DILG Central Office, thru her father, of the legalities of her situation. Therefore, any advice unheeded and the continuous holding of two positions in the government will tantamount to a misconduct on the part of Ms. Aldeguer. 3 DILG Opinion No 8, s. 2017 Page 3 of 4

Henceforth, kindly give us an update of the status of this case, and in the event of continuous disobedience of Ms. Aldeguer of this Department's advice, your Office can cause the filing of an administrative complaint against her with the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Cagayan de Oro City. This is in exercise of this Department's power of general supervision over LGUs. It is also suggested that you should inform the Regional Offices DepEd and CSC of this Department's opinion relative to the case of Ms. Aldeguer, for their appropriate action. We hope that we have addressed your concerns accordingly. ery truly you BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRET TIN B.D O Undersecretary Copy furnished: ENGR. JANE J.
